The test `testDigitLimitConstructor` in `BigFractionTest` is failing. The test is trying to initialize a `BigFraction` object with a value of `0.5000000001` and a maximum denominator of `10`. The current bug report mentions that an overflow exception is thrown when a `Fraction` is initialized with a `maxDenominator` from a `double` that is very close to a simple fraction.

Looking at the constructor `BigFraction(double value, int maxDenominator)` in the `BigFraction` class, it seems that the constructor delegates to another constructor `this(value, 0, maxDenominator, 100)`.

The issue seems to be related to the conversion of the `double` value to a `Fraction` when the `maxDenominator` is very close to a simple fraction. This may be causing an overflow exception during the construction of the `BigFraction` object.

To fix this issue, the conversion logic of the `double` value to a `Fraction` needs to be adjusted to handle cases where the `maxDenominator` is very close to a simple fraction.

Next, I will suggest the best locations to apply fixes.
```java
org.apache.commons.math3.fraction.BigFraction.<init>(double, int)
```
